name: No generic font stack (Inter / Roboto / Arial / system only)
source: NN/g 'AI Prototyping in Real Design Contexts' (nngroup.com/articles/ai-prototyping/) + NN/g 'First Impressions: 50ms' (nngroup.com/articles/first-impressions-human-automaticity/)
description: Detects when the page's body font-family stack consists entirely of overused fonts: Inter, Roboto, Arial, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, sans-serif.
rationale: NN/g's 2024-25 AI Prototyping study found AI tools 'share a similar, generic look' with 'sans-serif typeface, minimalist styling, flat and interchangeable appearance' because Inter and the system stack dominate the training data. Lindgaard's first-impressions research (50ms aesthetic judgment) and NN/g's recommendation of max ~2 fonts together justify treating the absence of a distinctive face as a measurable defect, not stylistic preference. Even loading a single distinctive font from Google Fonts demonstrates intent.
pass_criteria: The body font-family stack must contain at least one font NOT in the canonical generic list (Inter, Roboto, Arial, Helvetica, system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, sans-serif, serif, monospace).
